topics.title: What is a web page?
topics.explain: A web page is a file of code called HTML. Code is words that tell the computer what to show. A tag is a word in pointy brackets. Most tags come in two parts: one opens, and one with a slash closes.

Hello!

This is my first page.

is what you see on the page

topics.title: The bones of every page
topics.keywords: skeleton doctype head body title meta charset
topics.explain: Every page has the same bones. The first line says this is a web page. The head holds notes about the page, like its title. The body holds everything you see.

topics.title: How to use HTML Lab
topics.keywords: app tabs save open tab dot esc typing helpers view
topics.explain: Each file has a tab above the code, so click a tab to see that file. A dot on a tab means there are changes that are not saved. Press Save to keep them, and the dot goes away. The page below tells you more.

code.text:
Leaving the code

In the code, the Tab key makes spaces. To leave the code, press Esc, then Tab.

legend.means: is the key above Caps Lock
is at the top left of the keyboard

files.name: my-page.html
files.code:
Hello!

Leaving the code

In the code, the Tab key makes spaces. To leave the code, press Esc, then Tab.

Typing Helpers

They close tags and brackets for you, and suggest words. To practice writing them yourself, turn them off in the View menu, at the top of the screen.

Phone and Tablet

The little phone and tablet buttons above the page show it at those sizes. The computer button brings it back.

On a Finnish keyboard

A slash / is Shift+7. The curly brackets { and } are Alt+Shift+8 and Alt+Shift+9.

topics.title: Headings and paragraphs
topics.keywords: h1 h2 p text title h3 h4 h5 h6 heading paragraph
topics.explain: A heading is a title for one part of your page. h1 is the biggest heading, h2 is smaller, and so on down to h6. The p tag makes a paragraph, which is a block of text.

topics.title: Bold, italic and line breaks
topics.keywords: strong em br comment b i note
topics.explain: The strong tag makes words bold, which means thick and dark. The em tag makes words italic, which means they lean to the side. The br tag starts a new line, and it has no closing tag. A comment is a note to yourself that never shows on the page.

topics.keywords: a href link second page anchor click
topics.explain: A link is words you can click to go to another page. The a tag makes a link. Its href word says which page to open. Write the file name of that page there.

topics.title: Pictures
topics.keywords: img image picture photo file path src alt svg png jpg
topics.explain: The img tag shows a picture. Its src word names the file, and its alt word says what the picture shows. Save your project first. Then put the picture in the same folder.

topics.title: Pictures for the web
topics.keywords: webp jpg jpeg png svg avif gif format file type small fast width height lazy loading
topics.explain: Pick the right kind of picture file. A photo is best as JPG or WebP. A drawing, or a picture with a see-through part, is best as PNG or SVG. WebP files are small, so your page opens fast. Give each picture its width and height, so the page does not jump while it loads. AVIF is newer and even smaller, but older Macs cannot show it yet.

topics.title: Lists
topics.keywords: ul ol li list bullet numbered
topics.explain: A list shows things one under the other. The ul tag makes a list with dots. The ol tag makes a list with numbers. Each thing goes in its own li tag.

topics.title: Tables
topics.explain: A table puts things in rows and boxes. The tr tag makes a row, which is one line across. The td tag makes one box in that row. The th tag is a box for a heading, and its words are bold.

topics.title: Page sections
topics.keywords: header nav main footer div span section
topics.explain: These tags are boxes for the parts of your page. The header tag is the top, main is the middle, and footer is the bottom. The nav tag holds your links. The div tag is a plain box for anything, and span is a small box inside a line of text.

topics.title: Forms and buttons
topics.explain: A form is a place where people can type. The input tag makes a box to type in. The button tag makes a button to press. Buttons here do not send anything yet.

</form>

topics.keywords: font size family bold font-size font-family font-weight text-align center
topics.explain: A font is a style of letters. font-family picks the font, and font-size says how big the letters are. font-weight makes them thick. text-align moves them left, center or right.

topics.title: The box: margin, border, padding
topics.keywords: box space spacing margin-top margin-bottom margin-left margin-right padding-top padding-bottom padding-left padding-right

topics.keywords: hover transition animation keyframes mouse move
topics.explain: Hover means your mouse pointer is on a tag. A :hover style works only then. transition makes the change slow and smooth, and 1s means one second. @keyframes makes a tag move by itself.

    <title>My page</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <button>Press me</button>
  </body>
</html>
